article_title: Revisiting the trajectory of medical students' empathy, and impact of gender, specialty preferences and nationality: a systematic review.
citation: Andersen Freja Allerelli, Johansen Ann-Sofie Bering, Søndergaard Jens, Andersen Christina Maar, Assing Hvidt Elisabeth. (2020). Revisiting the trajectory of medical students' empathy, and impact of gender, specialty preferences and nationality: a systematic review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1964-5
title: Jefferson Scale of Empathy – Student Version (JSPE-S)
description: The JSPE-S is the self-report instrument used by most included studies; the review describes it as measuring affective empathy and studying "the empathic relationship between the medical student and the patient". It consists of 20 items on a 7-point Likert scale, with a minimum of 20 and a maximum of 140 points, where a high score indicates a more empathic orientation. All cross-sectional studies except four, and all longitudinal studies except one, employed the JSPE-S. The review notes the scale focuses on thoughts and not actions, citing Sulzer.
requirements: Validated scales; the review notes all studies except one employed validated scales, and flags one study applying the English validated JSPE-S to students without English as their native language
constraints: Self-reporting questionnaires introduce reporting bias; self-reported empathy has only a vague association with the patient-physician relationship in the clinical setting, per the review's cited literature
target_learning_goals: measuring empathy levels across educational years, gender, specialty preference and nationality
examples: Cross-sectional sample sizes of included studies using the JSPE-S ranged from 129 to 5521 participants, and longitudinal samples from 72 to 1653
key_sources: Andersen Freja Allerelli, Johansen Ann-Sofie Bering, Søndergaard Jens, Andersen Christina Maar, Assing Hvidt Elisabeth. (2020). Revisiting the trajectory of medical students' empathy, and impact of gender, specialty preferences and nationality: a systematic review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1964-5

article_title: Selecting for empathy? A cross-sectional study on empathy and empathic care intentions in newly enrolled dentistry, medicine, nursing, and pharmacy students in Singapore to inform admissions and training.
citation: Müller AM, Tan CGL, Lau STL, Gallagher PJ. (2026). Selecting for empathy? A cross-sectional study on empathy and empathic care intentions in newly enrolled dentistry, medicine, nursing, and pharmacy students in Singapore to inform admissions and training. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09510-2
title: Jefferson Scale of Empathy, Healthcare Professions Student version (JSE-HPS)
description: The JSE-HPS is a 20-item instrument rated on a 7-point Likert scale focusing on cognitive dimensions of empathy, described by the article as "a widely used and psychometrically robust instrument in healthcare education research". Total scores range from 20 to 140, with higher scores indicating greater empathy. The study used it to measure empathy among 646 newly enrolled healthcare students, yielding a median score of 109 (IQR: 102–116).
requirements: A licence for the instrument; the article notes funding was received for the licence of the JSE-HPS.
constraints: The article notes interpreting scores is challenging due to the absence of population-specific normative data across disciplines; published normative data have focused exclusively on Medicine students.
target_learning_goals: Assessment of cognitive empathy attitudes and beliefs related to patient-centred care
examples: The study administered the JSE-HPS to 646 newly enrolled Dentistry, Medicine, Nursing, and Pharmacy students via an online survey before and during the first weeks of the academic year.
key_sources: Müller AM, Tan CGL, Lau STL, Gallagher PJ. (2026). Selecting for empathy? A cross-sectional study on empathy and empathic care intentions in newly enrolled dentistry, medicine, nursing, and pharmacy students in Singapore to inform admissions and training. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09510-2

article_title: The effect of an empathy role-play program for operating room nursing students.
citation: Larti N, Ashouri E, Aarabi A. (2018). The effects of an empathy role-playing program for operating room nursing students in Iran. J Educ Eval Health Prof. https://doi.org/10.3352/jeehp.2018.15.29
title: Jefferson Scale of Empathy–Health Profession Students version (JSE-HPS) as the outcome measure
description: The JSE-HPS is a 20-item self-report questionnaire used as the study's outcome measure, scored on a 7-point Likert-type scale with total scores ranging from 20 to 140, where higher scores indicate more empathy with patients. It has 10 reverse-scored negative items and three sub-scales: perspective-taking (10 items), compassionate care (8 items), and standing in patient's shoes (2 items). In this study the Persian version's validity was confirmed by 10 faculty members and reliability was Cronbach alpha 0.71.
requirements: Administration before, immediately after, and 1 month after the intervention in this study
constraints: Test-retest reliability coefficients reported from prior work were 0.58 and 0.69 for 3- and 6-month intervals
target_learners: Health profession students, including operating room nursing students
examples: Participants completed the JSE-HPS as pretest in Session 1, as post-test 1 at the end of Session 3, and as post-test 2 one month later.
key_sources: Larti N, Ashouri E, Aarabi A. (2018). The effects of an empathy role-playing program for operating room nursing students in Iran. J Educ Eval Health Prof. https://doi.org/10.3352/jeehp.2018.15.29

article_title: Mod\`eles de jeux s\'erieux collaboratifs et mobiles
citation: Iza Marfisi-Schottman, Sébastien George. (2015). Modèles de jeux sérieux collaboratifs et mobiles. Actes de la Conférence Environnements Informatiques pour l'Apprentissage Humain, Agadir, Maroc. http://www.rewild.fr
title: Synergy framework linking collaboration, game mechanics and mobility in mobile collaborative serious games
description: The article proposes an analytical framework, represented in Fig. 1, of the pairwise synergies between collaboration, game mechanics and mobility in learning games. Dashed arrows represent the synergies between the three mechanisms while "Les flèches pleines représentent les effets de ces mécaniques sur l'apprentissage". Examples include complementary roles forcing learners to defend viewpoints, GPS/accelerometer feedback used to adapt the game, and physically dispersed teammates making collaboration more stimulating.
requirements: Game scenarios must be designed so that all participants contribute and roles, tools and movement are interdependent
constraints: The authors state that design of such applications remains experimental, without a method to guarantee maximal synergy
target_learners: school and higher-education students using mobile devices
examples: Environmental Detective assigns complementary roles (construction-company employee, environmental activist); Disease Simulation has children wear lights showing infection and spread the virus by proximity; Rewild motivates beginner hikers to climb mountains with in-game rewards
key_sources: Iza Marfisi-Schottman, Sébastien George. (2015). Modèles de jeux sérieux collaboratifs et mobiles. Actes de la Conférence Environnements Informatiques pour l'Apprentissage Humain, Agadir, Maroc. http://www.rewild.fr

article_title: Mod\`eles de jeux s\'erieux collaboratifs et mobiles
citation: Iza Marfisi-Schottman, Sébastien George. (2015). Modèles de jeux sérieux collaboratifs et mobiles. Actes de la Conférence Environnements Informatiques pour l'Apprentissage Humain, Agadir, Maroc. http://www.rewild.fr
title: Live-action role-play (GN) pattern for mobile collaborative serious games
description: A game pattern built around rule-guided role-play in which players choose their character's actions according to objectives and alliances, creating "une infinité d'histoires possible pour le jeu". A game master, typically the teacher, orchestrates play, keeps scores, observes learners and adapts the game. The authors judge GN particularly suited to improving social skills such as communication and negotiation and to understanding complex multi-actor topics; a variant with minimal roles creates participatory simulations like Disease Simulation.
requirements: A game master to facilitate play and keep scores
complementary roles with role-specific scoring mechanics that force negotiation
target_learning_goals: arguing a viewpoint from collected data
examples: Example 1: a highway-construction debate where the mayor, citizens, shopkeepers, activists and two journalists with opposing stances must negotiate a solution satisfying all roles, gathering pro and con evidence on site and defending positions at general assemblies
key_sources: Iza Marfisi-Schottman, Sébastien George. (2015). Modèles de jeux sérieux collaboratifs et mobiles. Actes de la Conférence Environnements Informatiques pour l'Apprentissage Humain, Agadir, Maroc. http://www.rewild.fr

article_title: Mod\`eles de jeux s\'erieux collaboratifs et mobiles
citation: Iza Marfisi-Schottman, Sébastien George. (2015). Modèles de jeux sérieux collaboratifs et mobiles. Actes de la Conférence Environnements Informatiques pour l'Apprentissage Humain, Agadir, Maroc. http://www.rewild.fr
title: Investigation game pattern for mobile collaborative serious games
description: A pattern whose scenario is built around "une énigme centrale que les joueurs doivent résoudre en collectant et analysant des" information, closely similar to case-based learning. Learners are placed in the decision-maker's position on a realistic problem, which the authors judge ideal for training them to apply theoretical knowledge to concrete cases across a wide variety of competences. Mobility is used to move between rooms and scan QR codes to obtain documents and interviews, with teacher-led debriefing sessions.
requirements: A central enigma inspired by a real situation
time pressure and task division so teams of players must organise and share tasks
target_learners: higher-education and vocational students working in groups of three
target_learning_goals: applying theoretical knowledge to concrete cases
using decision-making tools such as brainstorming and criteria grids
examples: Example 2: 'Trois heures pour sauver Kogatana' — students hired by a company must identify the cause of recent money losses within limited time, scanning QR codes in different rooms to obtain documents and employee interview videos, with regular teacher debriefings
key_sources: Iza Marfisi-Schottman, Sébastien George. (2015). Modèles de jeux sérieux collaboratifs et mobiles. Actes de la Conférence Environnements Informatiques pour l'Apprentissage Humain, Agadir, Maroc. http://www.rewild.fr

article_title: Mod\`eles de jeux s\'erieux collaboratifs et mobiles
citation: Iza Marfisi-Schottman, Sébastien George. (2015). Modèles de jeux sérieux collaboratifs et mobiles. Actes de la Conférence Environnements Informatiques pour l'Apprentissage Humain, Agadir, Maroc. http://www.rewild.fr
title: Treasure hunt pattern for mobile collaborative serious games
description: A pattern in which players search for one or more hidden objects using a series of clues. Because this type of game incites players to explore and appropriate the physical environment, the authors judge it particularly suited to teaching the characteristics of real objects in their natural contexts. Collaboration enters through task distribution to collect items in time and through contact between teammates to decide strategy when resources run short.
requirements: A list of objects to find in the physical environment
shared resources or constraints that force teammates to communicate
target_learning_goals: characteristics of real objects in natural contexts
historical and cultural knowledge tied to a place
examples: Example 3: 'La soirée de Bacchus' — players explore the ruins of Pompeii to find drinks, food, guests and entertainment listed by Bacchus with insufficient gold, facing a moral choice between low satisfaction or stealing, before the volcano erupts either way
key_sources: Iza Marfisi-Schottman, Sébastien George. (2015). Modèles de jeux sérieux collaboratifs et mobiles. Actes de la Conférence Environnements Informatiques pour l'Apprentissage Humain, Agadir, Maroc. http://www.rewild.fr
